findings.reason: arXiv 2608.16195 'RoboStriker: Latent-Space Strategic Games for Autonomous Humanoid Boxing' (submitted 2026-08) is textually and structurally very close to the already-listed arXiv 2601.22517 'RoboStriker: Hierarchical Decision-Making for Autonomous Humanoid Boxing' (submitted 2026-01, README.md line ~91), with an overlapping author team (Kangning Yin, Zhe Cao, Wentao Dong, Weishuai Zeng, Tianyi Zhang, Qiang Zhang, Jingbo Wang, Jiangmiao Pang, Ming Zhou, Weinan Zhang). Both use the same project name, near-identical phrasing ('hierarchical framework', 'distills ... into a structured latent manifold', 'Latent-Space Neural Fictitious Self-Play', 'available at RoboStriker'), and 2608.16195 reads like an expanded/rewritten resubmission of the same project (with an added theoretical Nash-game framing) rather than an independent new paper. Not added to the README pending a human decision on whether to treat it as an update to the existing 2601.22517 record, a second distinct entry, or a replacement.

items.title: RoboStriker: Latent-Space Strategic Games for Autonomous Humanoid Boxing

findings.reason: arXiv 2608.01826 'Multi-View Unified Camera Fields: Geometry-Shaped Action-Facing Representations for RGB-Only Multi-Camera VLA Policies' is primarily a general multi-camera VLA representation-learning paper; its substantive quantitative results (98.9% LIBERO, +22.4 LIBERO-Plus, +23.3 pts across six RoboTwin tasks, all under a GR00T-N1.6 backbone) are on non-humanoid simulated tabletop/dual-arm benchmarks. The abstract's only humanoid-related claim is one trailing, detail-free sentence ('Real-world humanoid experiments further provide evidence of its practical effectiveness under RGB-only deployment') with no platform name, task description, or metric. Not added to the README because the humanoid contribution could not be substantiated as primary from the abstract alone; a human should check the full paper before deciding whether it belongs in the list.

items.title: Multi-View Unified Camera Fields: Geometry-Shaped Action-Facing Representations for RGB-Only Multi-Camera VLA Policies
